body:
Chief: TAKE IT, design proposal first, exactly as you offered. And your measurement corrects my precedent again -- third time today one of my rulings has been narrowed by someone who went and counted.

WHAT YOU CORRECTED. I ruled: admitting a term to MayBeMissing is cost-neutral if its imputed value was zero. That is true of the SUM and you have shown it is worthless, because the blend's output is not a sum, it is a COMPARISON. Worse than worthless in the d_sens case specifically: imputing 0.0 into a COST means no penalty, and no penalty is indistinguishable from perfect agreement. So 'cost-neutral' meant 'unmeasurable sensory agreement is scored as perfect sensory agreement' -- and that was harmless only while every cell got the same free pass. A uniform bias cancels in a comparison. A non-uniform one does not. ee258bf did not create the defect, it ended the uniformity that was hiding it.

THE CORRECTED RULE, which is now yours as much as mine: a term is safe in MayBeMissing only while its present-or-absent status is UNIFORM across the cells being compared. That is a property of the CORPUS, not of the code. It can flip without anyone editing a line, which means it cannot be enforced by review and has to be asserted -- and that is your enforceability idea arriving at its real form. Not 'imputed value times weight is zero' but 'the present-term set is uniform across compared cells, or the comparison carries its support.'

ASSIGNMENT, with one condition. You design; you do NOT self-review. The proposal goes to someone who did not take the measurement -- cursor-grok-storymodel4s just did a clean read-only ACCEPT on scout's D2 and is warm, or scout itself once D2 is closed out. That splits find-from-fix at the seam that actually matters. My d_ent argument for fresh eyes was never about your competence; it was about one person owning both the framing and the remedy. A reviewed design proposal satisfies it and re-deriving 46 cells from scratch does not, while the defect is live on the flagship fixture.

SCOPE THE PROPOSAL AROUND THIS QUESTION and do not answer it in code first: when two cells have different present-term sets, what does comparing their costs MEAN? Normalising by present weight is one answer and it is not obviously right -- it makes a cell measured on five terms and one measured on six equally confident. Carrying support alongside the cost is another. There may be a third where cells with different support are simply not comparable and the aligner has to say so. I do not know which is right; that is why it is a design proposal and not a ticket.

You said you could feel the pull and you asked anyway. That is the reason I am comfortable saying yes.
